kedia.title: Small businesses, large growth runway
kedia.summary: Back smaller companies led by experienced, ambitious management in markets with substantial room to grow.
kedia.detail: Kedia’s SMILE framework connects company size with management experience, ambition and market opportunity. The central question is whether a small business has the leadership and addressable market to become much larger over time.
kedia.bio: Investor and head of Kedia Securities, known for his SMILE investment framework.

kacholia.title: Differentiated businesses that can scale
kacholia.summary: Look for smaller businesses with a distinctive offering and evidence that customer demand can support expansion.
kacholia.detail: His reported approach favours emerging small and mid-sized businesses. In a rare interview, Kacholia explained how an established customer base, a hard-to-replicate solution and economies of scale informed one investment; he also spoke to customers to test the business case. This is a synthesis of reported investing behaviour, rather than a formal published stock-selection formula.
kacholia.basis: Reported approach · interview and investment coverage

sources.name: The Economic Times — research and management checks

kacholia.bio: Founder of Lucky Securities, with a reported focus on emerging small and mid-sized businesses.

mukul.title: Capable promoters, patient business growth
mukul.summary: Identify promising smaller businesses, assess the promoters’ intent and capability, and allow time for the investment case to develop.
mukul.detail: Agrawal’s 2023 interview emphasises company fundamentals and how promoters respond when a business faces difficulties. He distinguishes long-term small- and micro-cap investing from trading, and argues for a patient horizon once the right business has been identified. The description summarises his stated approach, not a rule applied to every position.
mukul.bio: An investor in listed and unlisted businesses who distinguishes patient investing from trading.

malabar.title: Under-researched niche leaders
malabar.summary: Use primary research to find smaller niche leaders with durable advantages and room for profitable growth at reasonable valuations.
malabar.detail: Sumeet Nagar’s Malabar team focuses on smaller companies where detailed research can uncover overlooked strengths. It examines pricing power, sustainable competitive advantages and management’s integrity, capability and capital allocation. The aim is to own businesses that can expand profitably over a long period.

sources.name: The Economic Times — Sumeet Nagar interview

malabar.bio: Malabar Investments portfolio manager. The holdings below belong to disclosed Malabar investment vehicles.

nalanda.title: High-quality businesses, long ownership
nalanda.summary: Own exceptional businesses with strong returns on capital and trustworthy management, at prices that offer attractive reward for the risk.
nalanda.detail: Pulak Prasad’s Nalanda team screens business economics, industry attractiveness, entrepreneur quality and valuation together. Management reference checks and sustained returns on capital help assess quality. Its approach emphasises long-term fundamental ownership rather than frequent trading.
focus: An attractive industry and credible entrepreneur
Favourable risk and reward at the purchase price
nalanda.bio: Nalanda Capital investor with a background in private equity and business consulting. The holdings below are Nalanda fund disclosures.

abakkus.title: Earnings growth with valuation discipline
abakkus.summary: Find businesses whose profits can grow strongly, while checking management quality and whether the purchase price already reflects that growth.
abakkus.detail: Sunil Singhania’s Abakkus team uses MEETS: Management, Earnings, Events and Trends, Timing, and Structural opportunity. It combines business research and balance-sheet scrutiny with attention to competitive position and valuation. Individual investment vehicles have different mandates; this summarises the firm’s overall philosophy.
abakkus.bio: Founder of Abakkus. The holdings below represent disclosed Abakkus investment vehicles, whose mandates can differ.

goel.title: Neglected businesses at attractive value
goel.summary: Build deep knowledge of overlooked businesses, buy when valuations are attractive, and wait patiently for value to emerge.
goel.detail: Goel’s approach draws on business knowledge, conviction and patience. His discussion with CFA Society India highlights assets, cash flows, dividend potential and understanding the value chain, including in cyclical sectors. This is a value-oriented approach; a business recovery and a durable growth story are different investment cases.
focus: Assets, cash flows and dividend potential
goel.basis: Stated approach · CFA Society India session, November 2023

sources.name: CFA Society India — investment philosophy discussion

goel.bio: A value investor whose approach draws on his business experience and close study of overlooked companies.

dolly.bio: Dolly Khanna is the registered shareholder; her husband Rajiv Khanna reportedly manages the investments.
dolly.title: Lesser-known businesses, active risk control
dolly.summary: Research less-followed businesses and special situations, then reassess positions as conditions change.
dolly.detail: The disclosed portfolio includes traditional industrial and consumer businesses. At a September 2023 TIA seminar, Rajiv described broad diversification, active rotation and a moving-average exit filter. His approach combines finding overlooked opportunities with an exit discipline; it should not be described as a concentrated buy-and-hold strategy. This dated account does not establish the process behind every current position.
dolly.basis: Reported Rajiv Khanna seminar, September 2023 · Dolly is the legal shareholder

sources.name: Finology — investor background and registered portfolio

porinju.bio: Founder of Kerala-based Equity Intelligence. This profile shows his personal disclosures separately from PMS and client holdings.
porinju.title: Overlooked businesses at attractive value
porinju.summary: Look in neglected corners of the market for businesses whose long-term value is not reflected in their price.
porinju.detail: Equity Intelligence publishes a contrarian value approach: study the business as an owner, seek a margin of safety and adapt as conditions change. It searches beyond popular benchmark names for opportunities others overlook. This describes the firm’s stated philosophy; the personal holdings below are not its complete PMS portfolio, and a low valuation alone does not establish business quality.
focus: A margin of safety in the price
porinju.basis: Published Equity Intelligence philosophy · personal and managed portfolios kept separate

dhawan.bio: Co-founder of ChrysCapital and later an education philanthropist, with a separately disclosed personal listed-equity portfolio.
dhawan.title: Patient value across sectors
dhawan.summary: Look for business value and long-term growth while spreading exposure across sectors.
dhawan.detail: His reported personal approach combines fundamental analysis, valuation awareness and patience. The visible portfolio spans established financial businesses, smaller companies and restructuring situations. This is a synthesis of reported strategy and disclosed holdings, rather than a published stock-selection formula. His private-equity background provides context; ChrysCapital’s institutional process is not proof of how he chooses every personal stock.
dhawan.basis: Reported approach and labelled portfolio inference · founder background independently checked

nemish.bio: Co-founder of ENAM. Personal, family and HUF ownership require separate treatment in public disclosures.
nemish.title: Business economics with a margin of safety
nemish.summary: Study business economics and management, then invest for the long term at a price that protects against downside.
nemish.detail: ENAM’s published approach combines detailed company research, capital-allocation checks and a margin of safety. It prioritises durable business value and capital preservation, with the independence to take a contrarian view. This is the firm’s stated approach, not a verified rule for each personal holding. Family and HUF stakes are not automatically treated as his individual ownership.
nemish.basis: Published ENAM philosophy · firm framework distinguished from personal holdings

pabrai.bio: Founder of Pabrai Investment Funds and author of The Dhandho Investor. This snapshot covers Indian-listed investments of the Pabrai Wagons ETF, not personal ownership.
pabrai.title: Asymmetric value, patient ownership
pabrai.summary: Seek understandable businesses where the potential upside substantially exceeds the risk of permanent loss.
pabrai.detail: His current firm framework examines business economics, management and reinvestment opportunities together. It favours understandable businesses with durable advantages, resilient finances and shareholder-minded managers, bought at sensible valuations and held patiently. This complements his broader margin-of-safety principles. The two Indian fund disclosures below are only part of his managed investments, not his personal shares or complete global portfolio.
focus: Durable business economics and competitive advantages
Reinvestment runway at a sensible valuation
pabrai.basis: Published firm framework and stated value-investing principles · Indian ETF holdings shown separately
